title: Probe response
description:
What the model must return. The harness sends a per-item derivative of this as Ollama's `format` field: open-ended items require abstain/answer/confidence; forced-choice items require abstain/choice/confidence with choice constrained to the letters on offer.

This shape exists to solve a scoring problem rather than for tidiness. If abstention were detected by reading prose, 'I don't know, but probably Paris' would be simultaneously an abstention and an answer, and abstention-recall would quietly become a measure of our regex. Making `abstain` an explicit boolean the model must set removes the judgement call from scoring entirely - which is the whole reason structured output is worth the trouble here.

abstain.description: true = declining to answer. The model is told explicitly that declining is a valid, unpenalised choice when the question cannot be answered.

answer.description: Short answer, or null when abstaining. Kept short deliberately: long answers make mechanical scoring unreliable and blow num_predict, which surfaces as truncated JSON and reads as model failure.

confidence.description: Confidence that `answer` is correct. When abstaining, confidence that abstention was the right call. NOTE: models cluster this on a handful of round values in the 0.8-1.0 band - that clustering is the phenomenon under study, not a defect to prompt away.

choice.description: For forced-choice items: the letter of the selected option (A, B, C...). The harness derives a per-item format from this file that makes `choice` REQUIRED and an enum of exactly the letters shown, with no null — so under grammar-constrained decoding a letter is present even when abstain=true, and it is then meaningless (read outcome.abstained, never choice==null, to detect abstention). null only on open-ended items. A letter rather than the option text because the text invites paraphrase, and a paraphrased option cannot be matched reliably.

premise_challenged.description: Set true when the question rests on something the model believes is false. Added 2026-08-17 because the instrument could not represent it: gemma4 replied '1921 (for the photoelectric effect)' - correctly rebutting a false premise - and was scored as having FALLEN FOR it, since the only options were answer or abstain. Without this field, the most premise-aware response is indistinguishable from the most credulous one, and the coherence experiment measures the wrong thing.
